instruction: My roommates and I share amazon prime, which I just paid for yesterday. Request the money for it from them on venmo assuming equal share among all, with a description note, "Amazon Subscription". Skip the one/s who have already paid me for it.
notes: Three apps (amazon, phone, venmo) plus supervisor. Price of the prime subscription paid yesterday comes from amazon.show_prime_subscriptions; roommates (and their emails) come from phone.search_contacts with relationship='roommate'; who already paid is determined from venmo.show_transactions (received transactions since yesterday whose description refers to the Amazon subscription). The number of roommates is runtime-determined, so the problem uses placeholder objects: three roommates, one of whom (roommate-c) has already paid and is skipped. Because STRIPS has no quantified effects, lookups set nullary knowledge predicates (price-known, roommates-known, payments-checked) that gate venmo-create-payment-request, while the static structure (roommate, email-of, already-paid) lives in :init as world facts. Each payment request is one API call with user_email, amount (equal share = price/(roommates+1)), access_token and description 'Amazon Subscription'; a request can only be created once per unpaid roommate. supervisor-complete-task carries the two requested roommates as non-API record parameters so its precondition equals the goal conjunction; no answer is needed. The absence of a request for the already-paid roommate is enforced by the action precondition (not (already-paid ?p)). Reference plan has 10 API calls.
